text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — ran into a behavior when a running request hits a page eviction + remap. attn kernel assumes contiguous KV layout and we threw a KV_MISS mid-stream. sharing logs + brain dump, want tradeoff opinions.

sara: can you paste the minimal repro?

alex: sure, condensed log:```
REQ id=0x7f3a kernel=attn_opt shards=[0,2]
fetch page 42 -> hit
evict page 41 (pressure) -> remap page 42 to fragment set [42a,42b]
kernel tries to read contiguous slot 1024..2047 -> KV_MISS unhandled -> panic path
```

jamie: why would eviction occur while the request is in-flight? don't we pin pages for the duration of a request?

priya: we pin but pin granularity is per-page and we use a soft pin with timeout. under heavy memory pressure + preemption the GC path can unpin and evict. also fragmentation (splitting pages into smaller blocks for IO) can make the original contiguous mapping invalid.

mike: current kernel ABI assumes a logical contiguous backing for the KV cache. two directions: (A) runtime presents a virtual contiguous view via indirection (no ABI change to kernels), or (B) evolve kernel ABI to accept scatter-gather KV slices (bigger ABI refactor but zero-copy friendly).

alex: indirection idea = runtime maintains page indirection table (logical_index -> physical fragment list). at read time runtime either returns a pointer if contiguous or performs a merge/read into a temp buffer and hands a pointer to the kernel. avoids changing kernels immediately.

sara: merge into temp buffer = copy cost on the hot path. can we use non-copy by mapping fragments into a contiguous vma (mmap + remap)? TLB/VM churn might still be cheaper than memcpy for large contexts.

mike: agreed. on linux we could use remap_file_pages or mmap + mremap tricks when fragments are page-aligned. downside: complexity + portability (mac/windows).

jamie: second option (scatter-gather ABI) forces every kernel to iterate fragment lists. huge churn across kernel implementations and optimizations. but long-term clean.

priya: also an operational fallback option: mark kernels with capability flags (e.g., "sg_friendly": true/false). runtime routes requests to sg-capable kernels when fragmentation is present, otherwise use optimized kernels. that buys time for ABI migration.

alex: +1. we should surface metrics: mid-request-evictions, remap_count, kernel_fallbacks. need dashboards and alerting so we don't silently take the slow path.

jamie: what about correctness edges like deterministic tokenization and function-calling? fallback must preserve deterministic output. if we route to a different kernel, results must match within acceptable deltas or we must gate rollout.

mike: propose a 3-step plan for RFC patch: (1) runtime indirection table + page-pin-with-timeout tuning + a temporary copy-path for fragmented reads; (2) kernel capability bit "sg_friendly" + routing logic; (3) telemetry + dashboard + canary rollout. After that we can iterate on mmap-based zero-copy or full ABI change.

priya: for (1) we should also add a fast-path check: if fragment count == 1 return direct pointer, if fragments <= 2 attempt remap, otherwise copy. heuristics based on fragment size distribution.

alex: I'll draft the RFC with those sections. Perf study needed: microbench copy vs remap vs sg iteration for our typical context lengths (512, 2048, 8192 tokens).

sara: can you add suggested metric names in RFC? my ops PR will wire them into console. e.g., `kv.mid_request_evictions`, `kv.fragment_remaps`, `kernel.fallback.rate`.

alex: noted. also: compatibility test matrix in RFC: kernel versions X.Y vs runtime 2.3 behavior. need unit tests that force mid-request eviction.

jamie: please include a short rollback plan and a default config to keep old behavior unless feature_flag enabled.

alex: will do, target RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. ack if you want to be a reviewer. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll review and add perf numbers.

priya: I'll draft the dashboard tiles and an alert rule.

infra-bot: deployment note: perf test harness job #4287 queued for 1782346000, will run with ATTN kernel variants.

alex: sweet, thanks everyone.
